news.title: Struggling to make its voice heard: Can the EU forge a true foreign policy?

But ever since that post was created, rivalries between different centres of power have diluted the EU's ability to speak with one voice. We saw that recently with tensions over who should represent the EU in any potential talks with Russia.

news.title: Strength of Meloni less linked to policy, more about her party's dominance within govt coalition
news.summary: William Hilderbrandt is pleased to welcome Dr. Giulia Sandri, Associate researcher at the Free University of Brussels. Meloni has benefited from something historically scarce in Italian politics: longevity. Four years of governmental stability have allowed her to accumulate diplomatic relationships, strengthening Italy’s position within Europe and giving Rome greater visibility internationally. Yet Sandri argues that this political success sits alongside a much less decisive domestic record. Improvements in employment and fiscal credibility coexist with weak growth, stagnant wages, declining purchasing power and persistent structural problems in healthcare, education, demographics and public administration.

news.title: Unearthing her story: The rise of women archaeologists

In the last 30 years, women have come to make up more than half of the profession. At the same time, advances in technology – from DNA analysis to carbon dating – are allowing archaeologists to build a far more accurate picture of the past. And sometimes, that means questioning assumptions that have existed for generations.

Forced displacement of civilians in occupied territory is considered a war crime under the Geneva Conventions.

news.title: 'Moroccans are desperate: Years of political crackdown and lack of economic opportunities'
news.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Aida Alami, New York Times World contributor. Drawing on her own field reporting at the Moroccan border, Alami challenges attempts to explain the mass crossing primarily through a theory of deliberate state orchestration. While acknowledging both Morocco’s history of leveraging migration in its relations with Spain and the possibility that security forces made tactical decisions on the day, Alami insists on distinguishing evidence from inference. Her reporting instead points toward an interaction between online misinformation, overwhelmed security forces, and a population already primed to migrate by political repression and limited economic opportunity.

news.title: New fears of oil supply disruption as US-Iran hostilities resume
news.summary: Renewed hostilities between the United States and Iran have brought back fears of oil supply disruption. Prices are on track for their steepest weekly gain since mid-July, up 7.6%, as the US-Iran war enters its seventh month. Twenty-five percent of the world's oil supply comes through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been blocked since the beginning of the war. FRANCE 24's international affairs editor Philip Turle gives more details.

news.title: From forced labour to World Heritage: Sao Tome's colonial plantations
news.summary: Sao Tome and Principe's "Rocas" – colonial-era plantations – have been added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in July 2026, in recognition of their architecture and their fundamental importance to the country’s history. While the majority of them now lie derelict, they are attracting increasing interest from investors keen to develop the tourism potential of the history-steeped buildings.

news.title: Israel takes its war on Palestine into the AI age
news.summary: The Hanover affair exposes a new front in Israel’s long-running effort to shape how Palestinians are understood.

news.title: IOM ramps up emergency aid in Lake Chad as thousands flee Boko Haram
news.summary: More than 75,000 people have been newly displaced within Chad’s Lake Province following a resurgence in Boko Haram attacks in recent months. That is the latest figure from the International Organization for Migration, which is providing emergency assistance to meet their most immediate needs. Most of these tens of thousands of people have fled the islands of Lake Chad, seeking safety in towns and villages further away from the island areas. FRANCE 24's Harold Girard reports.

news.title: #Nepal: Two flood survivors rescued from hydropower tunnel
news.summary: In a video posted to social media on September 4, the Nepali #army announced it had rescued two workers trapped in a hydropower tunnel. The rescue brings hope of reaching over a dozen others thought to be trapped inside the tunnel. Both men were flown to a hospital in #Kathmandu. The floods killed more than 1,200 people, and over 5,000 are still missing.

news.title: Nepal flood aftermath: Zip lines carry medicine as survivors relive the horror
news.summary: Eight days after disastrous floods in Nepal, as the death toll continues to rise, survivors are left struggling to access basic necessities. The shortages are adding to the hardships of those living in temporary shelters after having lost homes and belongings. While some are focusing on ensuring food and medicine reach devastated areas, many are now left grappling with the psychological trauma of the disaster.

news.title: Italy weighs the results as Giorgia Meloni’s government sets a longevity record
news.summary: In a country where governments are famously short-lived, the perceived success of Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni has often been attributed to her survival skills rather than her accomplishments. The record is likely to boost the prime minister's image as Italy, which has had almost 70 governments over the past 80 years, gears up for a national vote in 2027, analysts say. But recent events have complicated her path to re-election.

news.title: Nigerian police arrest four suspects over alleged organ harvesting
news.summary: In Nigeria, the police have arrested four suspects over alleged organ harvesting. Two of the suspects are medical doctors who are accused of carrying out the surgeries to harvest the kidneys. The victims are mainly vulnerable and uneducated youths whose financial desperation is exploited to illegally harvest their kidney for transplant to patients who are often wealthy, as FRANCE 24’s Sam Olukoya reports.

news.title: Tigray's fragile recovery at risk as drone strikes reignite war fears
news.summary: Over the past month, drone strikes have hit several parts of Ethiopia's Tigray region, sparking fears of a renewed war. The last conflict left an estimated 600,000 people dead, making it the deadliest conflict of the 21st century. As the region has not yet rebuilt or recovered from that damage, health experts are warning of the potential impact on patients if another war were to break out. FRANCE 24's Tom Canetty reports.

news.title: German far-right's breakout moment? AfD party eyes outright win in regional election
news.summary: Could Europeans awaken next Monday to another shock bellwether moment? German voters could for the first time since World War II give an outright majority to a far-right party in regional elections. We ask about the AfD's push in Saxony-Anhalt and a charismatic lead candidate whose campaign strives to put charm above the vitriol usually associated with a party with pro-Nazi roots.

news.title: Why early warning signs of glacier collapse in Nepal were difficult to detect
news.summary: The glacier collapse that led to devastating flash floods across the Himalayan region of Nepal and its border with the Chinese autonomous region of Tibet on August 26 was preceded by early warning signs, experts say. But monitoring and emergency alert systems in the region are still insufficient to predict such disasters.

news.title: USS Lincoln crew hits the streets of Thailand's Pattaya after nine-month deployment
news.summary: US sailors and Marines streamed into the Thai resort city of Pattaya Thursday after a record-breaking nine months at sea. Local police said there had so far been no major incidents connected to the 5,000-strong contingent of US service members, though two sailors were sent back to the ship after a drunken bar brawl.

news.title: Volkswagen board approves plan to cut another 50,000 jobs
news.summary: The group - which includes Audi, Porsche, Skoda as well as the VW brand - plans to cut a total of 100,000 posts by 2030.

news.title: Rescatadas con vida dos personas nueve días después de las inundaciones en Nepal, que dejan casi 1.300 muertos
news.summary: Las autoridades de Nepal han anunciado este viernes el rescate con vida de dos personas que quedaron atrapadas en un túnel sepultado por la devastadora inundación registrada el 26 de agosto en el norte del país, en la frontera con China, una tragedia que deja ya cerca de 1.300 muertos, según el último balance.

news.title: Serbia inicia preparativos para el funeral de Ratko Mladic tras la llegada de su cadáver a Belgrado
news.summary: Las autoridades de Serbia han iniciado los preparativos para la celebración del funeral del excomandante serbobosnio Ratko Mladic, fallecido el 27 de agosto mientras cumplía pena en una cárcel de La Haya tras ser condenado por crímenes de guerra y contra la humanidad, después de la llegada el jueves de su cadáver al aeropuerto de la capital, Belgrado, en un avión gubernamental.
